s: judges and rulers (appointed by Moses) have ranks thousands, hundreds, fifties, tens
q: rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.

s: judges and rulers (appointed by Moses) judge small matters (at all times; hard cases go to Moses)
q: They judged the people at all times. They brought the hard cases to Moses, but every small matter they judged themselves.

s: Jethro's counsel on delegating judgment is given by Jethro
q: Listen now to my voice. I will give you counsel, and God be with you.

s: Jethro's counsel on delegating judgment was followed by Moses
q: So Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law, and did all that he had said.

s: Jethro's counsel on delegating judgment has purpose ease Moses' load so he can endure
q: So shall it be easier for you, and they shall share the load with you.

s: judging the people was performed by Moses (alone, from morning to evening, before the counsel)
q: On the next day, Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood around Moses from the morning to the evening.

s: Jethro returns to his own land (after Moses let him depart)
q: Moses let his father-in-law depart, and he went his way into his own land.

s: Jethro is father in law of Moses
q: Now Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-law

s: Jethro is priest of Midian
q: Now Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-law

s: Moses has wife Zipporah
q: Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, received Zipporah, Moses’ wife

s: Moses has son Gershom (named for living as a foreigner in a foreign land)
q: The name of one son was Gershom, for Moses said, “I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign land”.

s: Moses has son Eliezer (named for God's help and deliverance from Pharaoh's sword)
q: The name of the other was Eliezer, for he said, “My father’s God was my help and delivered me from Pharaoh’s sword.”

s: Moses encamps at Mountain of God (in the wilderness)
q: to Moses into the wilderness where he was encamped, at the Mountain of God.

s: Moses leads children of Israel (judges the people and teaches them God's statutes)
q: When they have a matter, they come to me, and I judge between a man and his neighbor, and I make them know the statutes of God, and his laws.”

s: LORD delivered children of Israel (out of Egypt and from the Egyptians)
q: how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.

s: children of Israel encamps at wilderness of Sinai (before the mountain)
q: When they had departed from Rephidim, and had come to the wilderness of Sinai, they encamped in the wilderness; and there Israel encamped before the mountain.

s: children of Israel promises LORD (all the people answered together to do all he has spoken)
q: All the people answered together, and said, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do.”

s: theophany at Sinai occurs on Mount Sinai (on the third day)
q: for on the third day the LORD will come down in the sight of all the people on Mount Sinai.

s: theophany at Sinai has feature thunders, lightnings, thick cloud and loud trumpet (morning of the third day)
q: there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of an exceedingly loud trumpet

s: Mount Sinai has state smoking and quaking (because the LORD descended on it in fire)
q: All of Mount Sinai smoked, because the LORD descended on it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked greatly.

s: theophany at Sinai has purpose people hear God speak with Moses and believe him (stated by the LORD)
q: Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also believe you forever.

s: boundary (around Mount Sinai) protects Mount Sinai (touching the mountain or its border is punishable by death)
q: You shall set bounds to the people all around, saying, ‘Be careful that you don’t go up onto the mountain, or touch its border. Whoever touches the mountain shall be surely put to death.

s: boundary (around Mount Sinai) is commanded to Moses
q: You shall set bounds to the people all around

s: Moses performs sanctification (of the people) (as the LORD commanded)
q: Moses went down from the mountain to the people, and sanctified the people

s: children of Israel departed from Rephidim
q: When they had departed from Rephidim, and had come to the wilderness of Sinai

s: Aaron accompanies Moses (permitted to come up the mountain)
q: You shall bring Aaron up with you

s: elders (of the people of Israel) represent children of Israel (Moses called them to hear the LORD's words)
q: Moses came and called for the elders of the people

s: Moses ascends Mount Sinai (called by the LORD to the top)
q: The LORD called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.

s: children of Israel went out of Egypt (arrived at Sinai in the third month)
q: In the third month after the children of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt, on that same day they came into the wilderness of Sinai.

s: LORD delivered children of Israel (bore them on eagles' wings)
q: how I bore you on eagles’ wings, and brought you to myself.

s: LORD acted against Egyptians (Israel saw what he did)
q: You have seen what I did to the Egyptians

s: children of Israel is own possession of LORD (conditional on obeying his voice and keeping his covenant)
q: if you will indeed obey my voice and keep my covenant, then you shall be my own possession from among all peoples; for all the earth is mine;

s: children of Israel is a kingdom of priests and a holy nation (promised status to the LORD)
q: and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.

s: LORD owns all the earth
q: for all the earth is mine;

s: Moses mediates for LORD (speaks the LORD's words to the people and reports the people's words)
q: Moses came and called for the elders of the people, and set before them all these words which the LORD commanded him.

s: LORD brought out Israelites (from Egypt, the house of bondage)
q: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

s: Israelites is commanded to have no other gods before the LORD
q: “You shall have no other gods before me.

s: Israelites is commanded to honor parents (your father and your mother) (so that their days may be long in the land)
q: “Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the LORD your God gives you.

s: Israelites fears LORD (stayed at a distance after seeing the mountain's thunder and smoke)
q: When the people saw it, they trembled, and stayed at a distance.

s: Moses serves as intermediary for Israelites (people asked him to speak with them instead of God)
q: They said to Moses, “Speak with us yourself, and we will listen; but don’t let God speak with us, lest we die.”

s: Moses approaches LORD (came near to the thick darkness where God was)
q: Moses came near to the thick darkness where God was.

s: idols and images is forbidden by the Ten Commandments (no idol or image of anything in heaven, earth or water)
q: “You shall not make for yourselves an idol, nor any image of anything that is in the heavens above, or that is on the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:

s: altar is made of earth (for burnt and peace offerings)
q: You shall make an altar of earth for me, and shall sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your cattle.

s: altar must not be built of cut stones (if made of stone)
q: If you make me an altar of stone, you shall not build it of cut stones; for if you lift up your tool on it, you have polluted it.

s: altar has no steps (to avoid exposing nakedness)
q: You shall not go up by steps to my altar, that your nakedness may not be exposed to it.’

s: LORD is jealous God
q: for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God

s: LORD shows loving kindness to those who love him and keep his commandments (to thousands)
q: and showing loving kindness to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.

s: LORD visits iniquity on children of those who hate him (third and fourth generation)
q: visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, on the third and on the fourth generation of those who hate me

s: LORD created heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them (in six days)
q: for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them

s: LORD blessed Sabbath (and made it holy)
q: therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day, and made it holy.

s: LORD does not hold guiltless one who misuses his name
q: for the LORD will not hold him guiltless who misuses his name.

s: Sabbath is a holy day (the seventh day, to the LORD)
q: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God.

s: Sabbath prohibits work (applies to household, servants, livestock and strangers)
q: You shall not do any work in it, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your livestock, nor your stranger who is within your gates;

s: Moses is a Hebrew (child of Hebrew parents)
q: “This is one of the Hebrews’ children.”

s: Moses' mother (woman of the house of Levi) belongs to Levi (daughter of Levi)
q: A man of the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi as his wife.

s: Moses' mother (woman of the house of Levi) has spouse Moses' father (man of the house of Levi)
q: A man of the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi as his wife.

s: Pharaoh's daughter has father Pharaoh
q: Pharaoh’s daughter came down to bathe at the river.

s: Pharaoh's daughter has servant servant (Pharaoh's daughter's servant)
q: sent her servant to get it

s: Pharaoh's daughter has maidens Pharaoh's daughter's maidens
q: Her maidens walked along by the riverside.

s: Reuel is a priest of Midian
q: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters.

s: Reuel has daughters daughters of Reuel (seven daughters)
q: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters.

s: Reuel owns flock (Reuel's flock)
q: to water their father’s flock

s: Zipporah has father Reuel
q: He gave Moses Zipporah, his daughter.

s: Israelites suffer under forced labor of Israelites (in Egypt)
q: the children of Israel sighed because of the bondage

s: Moses has mother Moses' mother (woman of the house of Levi) (birth mother)
q: The woman conceived and bore a son.

s: LORD has covenant with Abraham (covenant also with Isaac and Jacob)
q: God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

s: Moses' killing of the Egyptian has perpetrator Moses
q: he killed the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.

s: Moses' killing of the Egyptian has victim Egyptian (man Moses killed)
q: he killed the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.

s: Moses has sister Moses' sister
q: His sister stood far off, to see what would be done to him.

s: Moses has adoptive mother Pharaoh's daughter (adopted as her son)
q: he became her son. She named him Moses

s: Moses has name origin drawn out of the water (given by Pharaoh's daughter)
q: She named him Moses, and said, “Because I drew him out of the water.”

s: Moses lives in Midian (fled there from Pharaoh)
q: Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and lived in the land of Midian

s: Moses has spouse Zipporah
q: He gave Moses Zipporah, his daughter.

s: Moses has son Gershom
q: She bore a son, and he named him Gershom

s: Moses has father in law Reuel
q: Moses was content to dwell with the man. He gave Moses Zipporah, his daughter.

s: Hebrew servant serves for six years (goes out free in the seventh year without paying)
q: If you buy a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years, and in the seventh he shall go out free without paying anything.

s: homicide and violence penalty for attacking parents death
q: “Anyone who attacks his father or his mother shall be surely put to death.

s: homicide and violence penalty for kidnapping death
q: “Anyone who kidnaps someone and sells him, or if he is found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.

s: homicide and violence penalty for cursing parents death
q: “Anyone who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.

s: male servant and maid is property of master (basis for no punishment if servant recovers after a day or two)
q: Notwithstanding, if his servant gets up after a day or two, he shall not be punished, for the servant is his property.

s: male servant and maid goes free if eye or tooth destroyed by master (compensation for the injury)
q: If a man strikes his servant’s eye, or his maid’s eye, and destroys it, he shall let him go free for his eye’s sake.

s: lex talionis (eye for eye) prescribes life for life (if harm follows to the pregnant woman)
q: But if any harm follows, then you must take life for life,

s: lex talionis (eye for eye) includes eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot
q: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,

s: goring bull penalty stoned (when it gores a man or woman to death; its meat shall not be eaten)
q: the bull shall surely be stoned, and its meat shall not be eaten; but the owner of the bull shall not be held responsible.

s: owner of the bull is put to death if bull habitually gored and owner failed to keep it in (ransom may be imposed instead)
q: But if the bull had a habit of goring in the past, and this has been testified to its owner, and he has not kept it in, but it has killed a man or a woman, the bull shall be stoned, and its owner shall also be put to death.

s: owner of the bull pays to master thirty shekels of silver (if the bull gores a male or female servant)
q: If the bull gores a male servant or a female servant, thirty shekels of silver shall be given to their master, and the ox shall be stoned.

s: Hebrew servant is bought by master (of the Hebrew servant)
q: If you buy a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years

s: liability for animals and property holds pit owner liable pit owner pays money and keeps dead animal (when a bull or donkey falls into an uncovered pit)
q: the owner of the pit shall make it good. He shall give money to its owner, and the dead animal shall be his.

s: liability for animals and property rule for injured bull sell live bull and divide price and dead animal (when one man's bull kills another's)
q: then they shall sell the live bull, and divide its price; and they shall also divide the dead animal.

s: Hebrew servant leaves with wife wife (of the Hebrew servant) (if he is married when he comes in)
q: If he is married, then his wife shall go out with him.

s: master (of the Hebrew servant) retains ownership of wife (of the Hebrew servant) (when the master gave her to the servant; she and her children stay with the master)
q: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall be her master’s, and he shall go out by himself.

s: master (of the Hebrew servant) performs ear boring on Hebrew servant (if servant declares he will not go out free; servant then serves forever)
q: then his master shall bring him to God, and shall bring him to the door or to the doorpost, and his master shall bore his ear through with an awl, and he shall serve him forever.

s: daughter (sold as female servant) release rule does not go out as male servants do
q: If a man sells his daughter to be a female servant, she shall not go out as the male servants do.

s: daughter (sold as female servant) may be redeemed yes (if she does not please the master who married her to himself; he cannot sell her to a foreign people)
q: If she doesn’t please her master, who has married her to himself, then he shall let her be redeemed. He shall have no right to sell her to a foreign people, since he has dealt deceitfully with her.

s: daughter (sold as female servant) is entitled to food, clothing and marital rights (if master takes another wife; otherwise she goes free without paying)
q: If he takes another wife to himself, he shall not diminish her food, her clothing, and her marital rights.

s: homicide and violence penalty for killing a man death (one who strikes a man so that he dies)
q: “One who strikes a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death,

s: LORD is described as gracious (explains why he hears the cry of the poor)
q: It will happen, when he cries to me, that I will hear, for I am gracious.

s: alien must not be wronged or oppressed (because Israel were aliens in Egypt)
q: “You shall not wrong an alien or oppress him, for you were aliens in the land of Egypt.

s: widow and fatherless child must not be taken advantage of (command)
q: “You shall not take advantage of any widow or fatherless child.

s: neighbor receives double from thief (when thief found after theft of goods kept for him)
q: if the thief is found, he shall pay double.

s: neighbor is owed restitution for animals let loose into his field (from the best of the offender's field and vineyard)
q: he shall make restitution from the best of his own field, and from the best of his own vineyard.

s: stolen animals and livestock includes ox, donkey, sheep (double payment if found alive)
q: whether it is ox, donkey, or sheep, he shall pay double.

s: theft and restitution laws requires for condemned party double payment (he whom God condemns pays his neighbor)
q: He whom God condemns shall pay double to his neighbor.

s: theft and restitution laws requires for borrowed item injured restitution (when its owner is not with it)
q: If a man borrows anything of his neighbor’s, and it is injured, or dies, its owner not being with it, he shall surely make restitution.

s: LORD protects widow and fatherless child (hears their cry and punishes those who take advantage of them)
q: If you take advantage of them at all, and they cry at all to me, I will surely hear their cry;

s: LORD requires exclusive worship from holy men (sacrifice to any other god is punished by destruction)
q: “He who sacrifices to any god, except to the LORD only, shall be utterly destroyed.

s: LORD claims firstborn of sons (also firstborn of cattle and sheep, given on the eighth day)
q: You shall give the firstborn of your sons to me.

s: thief pays for stolen ox five oxen (if he kills or sells it)
q: he shall pay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.

s: thief pays for stolen sheep four sheep (if he kills or sells it)
q: he shall pay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.

s: thief pays if animal found alive double (stolen property found in his hand)
q: If the stolen property is found in his hand alive, whether it is ox, donkey, or sheep, he shall pay double.

s: thief is sold if he cannot make restitution (if he has nothing)
q: If he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.

s: thief has no bloodguilt for killer if struck dead while breaking in (before sunrise)
q: If the thief is found breaking in, and is struck so that he dies, there shall be no guilt of bloodshed for him.

s: LORD sends angel (to keep Israelites by the way and bring them to the prepared place)
q: Behold, I send an angel before you, to keep you by the way, and to bring you into the place which I have prepared.

s: children of Israel forbidden to bow to gods of the inhabitants
q: You shall not bow down to their gods, nor serve them

s: gods of the inhabitants is a snare (for Israelites who serve them)
q: if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.

s: inhabitants of the land (Canaan) includes Jebusites (with Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites)
q: the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite

s: inhabitants of the land (Canaan) may not dwell in land of Israelites (lest they cause sin)
q: They shall not dwell in your land, lest they make you sin against me

s: sabbatical year occurs in seventh year (land rests and lies fallow for the poor)
q: but the seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow, that the poor of your people may eat

s: Sabbath rest occurs on seventh day (after six days of work)
q: Six days you shall do your work, and on the seventh day you shall rest

s: Sabbath rest benefits alien (with ox, donkey and servant's son)
q: that your ox and your donkey may have rest, and the son of your servant, and the alien may be refreshed.

s: Feast of Unleavened Bread lasts seven days (in the month Abib)
q: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the time appointed in the month Abib

s: Feast of Unleavened Bread commemorates Egypt (exodus)
q: for in it you came out of Egypt

s: feast of harvest celebrates first fruits (of labors sown in the field)
q: the feast of harvest, the first fruits of your labors, which you sow in the field

s: LORD is enemy to enemy (if Israelites obey the angel's voice)
q: then I will be an enemy to your enemies, and an adversary to your adversaries.

s: feast of ingathering occurs at end of the year (when labors are gathered from the field)
q: the feast of ingathering, at the end of the year, when you gather in your labors out of the field.

s: justice and fair testimony laws prohibits bribe (because it blinds and perverts)
q: “You shall take no bribe, for a bribe blinds those who have sight and perverts the words of the righteous.

s: justice and fair testimony laws prohibits oppressing an alien
q: “You shall not oppress an alien

s: justice and fair testimony laws prohibits false report
q: “You shall not spread a false report.

s: LORD promises to bless bread and water (if Israelites serve him)
q: You shall serve the LORD your God, and he will bless your bread and your water, and I will take sickness away from among you.

s: LORD sets border Red Sea to sea of the Philistines (Israelites' territory)
q: I will set your border from the Red Sea even to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River

s: LORD drives out inhabitants of the land (Canaan) (little by little)
q: Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you have increased and inherit the land.

s: children of Israel serves LORD (commanded)
q: You shall serve the LORD your God

s: children of Israel was in Egypt (formerly aliens)
q: since you were aliens in the land of Egypt.

s: children of Israel forbidden to make covenant with gods of the inhabitants (also with the inhabitants)
q: You shall make no covenant with them, nor with their gods.

s: Moses writes book of the covenant (wrote all the LORD's words)
q: Moses wrote all the LORD’s words, then rose up early in the morning

s: Moses has servant Joshua
q: Moses rose up with Joshua, his servant

s: Moses has status sole approacher of the LORD (others worship from a distance)
q: Moses alone shall come near to the LORD, but they shall not come near.

s: Aaron has role dispute resolver for the elders (with Hur, while Moses is away)
q: Behold, Aaron and Hur are with you. Whoever is involved in a dispute can go to them.”

s: glory of the LORD settles on Mount Sinai
q: The LORD’s glory settled on Mount Sinai

s: cloud (on Mount Sinai) covers Mount Sinai (six days before the LORD called)
q: the cloud covered it six days.

s: two tablets of the covenant contains law and commands (written by the LORD)
q: I will give you the stone tablets with the law and the commands that I have written

s: Mount Sinai is called God's Mountain
q: Moses went up onto God’s Mountain.

s: Moses builds altar (Moses' altar) (at the base of the mountain)
q: built an altar at the base of the mountain, with twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.

s: blood of the covenant is a sign of the covenant (sprinkled on the people)
q: “Look, this is the blood of the covenant, which the LORD has made with you concerning all these words.”

s: covenant (between the LORD and Israel) made by LORD (concerning all these words)
q: which the LORD has made with you concerning all these words.

s: covenant (between the LORD and Israel) made with Israelites
q: which the LORD has made with you concerning all these words.

s: Israelites accepts covenant (between the LORD and Israel) (promised to do and obey all the LORD's words)
q: “We will do all that the LORD has said, and be obedient.”

s: LORD speaks to Moses (commissioning the offering)
q: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

s: pattern was shown on Mount Sinai (shown to Moses)
q: which has been shown to you on the mountain.

s: offering (for the tabernacle work) is taken from children of Israel (from everyone whose heart makes him willing)
q: From everyone whose heart makes him willing you shall take my offering.

s: offering (for the tabernacle work) includes gold (material)
q: gold, silver, bronze,

s: LORD meets with moses at mercy seat (speaks from between the two cherubim)
q: There I will meet with you, and I will tell you from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim which are on the ark of the covenant

s: lamp stand is made of gold (pure hammered gold, one piece, a talent)
q: You shall make a lamp stand of pure gold. The lamp stand shall be made of hammered work.

s: lamp stand has branches six (three on each side)
q: There shall be six branches going out of its sides: three branches of the lamp stand out of its one side, and three branches of the lamp stand out of its other side;

s: lamp stand has part lamps (seven, give light to the space in front of it)
q: You shall make its lamps seven, and they shall light its lamps to give light to the space in front of it.

s: lamp stand has accessories snuffers and snuff dishes of pure gold
q: Its snuffers and its snuff dishes shall be of pure gold.

s: lamp stand has weight a talent of pure gold (with all accessories)
q: It shall be made of a talent of pure gold, with all these accessories.

s: tabernacle (Tent of Meeting) is made with curtains of fine twined linen (tabernacle's ten curtains) (ten curtains)
q: you shall make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, with cherubim.

s: curtains of fine twined linen (tabernacle's ten curtains) is coupled in five and five (two sets of five)
q: Five curtains shall be coupled together to one another, and the other five curtains shall be coupled to one another.

s: curtains of fine twined linen (tabernacle's ten curtains) has part loops (fifty of blue on each coupling's edge)
q: You shall make fifty loops in the one curtain, and you shall make fifty loops in the edge of the curtain that is in the second coupling.

s: curtains of fine twined linen (tabernacle's ten curtains) is joined by clasps of gold (fifty clasps)
q: You shall make fifty clasps of gold, and couple the curtains to one another with the clasps.

s: curtains of goats' hair (covering over the tabernacle) has count eleven
q: You shall make eleven curtains.

s: curtains of goats' hair (covering over the tabernacle) has length thirty cubits (each curtain)
q: The length of each curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits

s: curtains of goats' hair (covering over the tabernacle) has width four cubits (each curtain)
q: The length of each curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits

s: curtains of goats' hair (covering over the tabernacle) is joined by clasps of bronze (fifty clasps into the loops)
q: You shall make fifty clasps of bronze, and put the clasps into the loops, and couple the tent together, that it may be one.

s: curtains of goats' hair (covering over the tabernacle) has part loops (fifty on each outermost edge)
q: You shall make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain that is outermost in the coupling, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain which is outermost in the second coupling.

s: curtains of goats' hair (covering over the tabernacle) covers tabernacle (Tent of Meeting) (covering over it)
q: You shall make curtains of goats’ hair for a covering over the tabernacle.

s: boards (of the tabernacle) has length ten cubits (each board)
q: Ten cubits shall be the length of a board, and one and a half cubits the width of each board.

s: tabernacle (Tent of Meeting) has pattern shown on mountain (set up according to the way shown)
q: You shall set up the tabernacle according to the way that it was shown to you on the mountain.

s: boards (of the tabernacle) has width one and a half cubits (each board)
q: Ten cubits shall be the length of a board, and one and a half cubits the width of each board.

s: boards (of the tabernacle) has part tenons (two in each board)
q: There shall be two tenons in each board, joined to one another

s: boards (of the tabernacle) stands on sockets of silver (two sockets under each board)
q: two sockets under one board for its two tenons, and two sockets under another board for its two tenons.

s: boards (of the tabernacle) has count twenty (south side)
q: You shall make twenty boards for the tabernacle, for the south side southward.

s: boards (of the tabernacle) has count eight (west side, including two corner boards)
q: There shall be eight boards, and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets

s: boards (of the tabernacle) is overlaid with gold
q: You shall overlay the boards with gold, and make their rings of gold for places for the bars.

s: boards (of the tabernacle) has part rings of gold (places for the bars)
q: make their rings of gold for places for the bars.

s: boards (of the tabernacle) is held by bars of acacia wood (middle bar passes end to end)
q: The middle bar in the middle of the boards shall pass through from end to end.

s: veil is made of blue, purple, scarlet, fine twined linen (with cherubim, skillful workman)
q: You shall make a veil of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, with cherubim.

s: veil hangs on pillars for the veil (four pillars of acacia overlaid with gold, on four silver sockets)
q: You shall hang it on four pillars of acacia overlaid with gold; their hooks shall be of gold, on four sockets of silver.

s: tabernacle (Tent of Meeting) has part clasps of gold (couple the curtains into a unit)
q: You shall make fifty clasps of gold, and couple the curtains to one another with the clasps. The tabernacle shall be a unit.

s: veil separates holy place (from the most holy place)
q: The veil shall separate the holy place from the most holy for you.

s: veil has decoration cherubim (on the mercy seat)

s: ark of the covenant is located in most holy place (within the veil)
q: shall bring the ark of the covenant in there within the veil.

s: ark of the covenant has part mercy seat (placed on the ark)
q: You shall put the mercy seat on the ark of the covenant in the most holy place.

s: table is located north side of the tabernacle (outside the veil)
q: You shall set the table outside the veil, and the lamp stand opposite the table on the side of the tabernacle toward the south. You shall put the table on the north side.

s: lamp stand is located south side of the tabernacle (opposite the table)
q: the lamp stand opposite the table on the side of the tabernacle toward the south.

s: tabernacle (Tent of Meeting) has part boards (of the tabernacle) (standing upright)
q: “You shall make the boards for the tabernacle of acacia wood, standing upright.

s: tabernacle (Tent of Meeting) has part bars of acacia wood (five per side: south, north, west)
q: You shall make bars of acacia wood: five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,

s: tabernacle (Tent of Meeting) has part coverings of rams' skins and sea cow hides (covering for the tent)
q: You shall make a covering for the tent of rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering of sea cow hides above.

s: curtains of fine twined linen (tabernacle's ten curtains) has length twenty-eight cubits (each curtain)
q: The length of each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits

s: curtains of fine twined linen (tabernacle's ten curtains) has width four cubits (each curtain)
q: The length of each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits

s: curtains of fine twined linen (tabernacle's ten curtains) has decoration cherubim (on the mercy seat) (work of a skillful workman)
q: with cherubim. You shall make them with the work of a skillful workman.

s: altar is made of acacia wood (overlaid with bronze)
q: You shall make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long, and five cubits wide.

s: court (around the tabernacle) has length one hundred cubits

s: court (around the tabernacle) is part of tabernacle (Tent of Meeting)
q: You shall make the court of the tabernacle

s: altar has length five cubits
q: You shall make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long, and five cubits wide.

s: court (around the tabernacle) has part hangings (court of the tabernacle) (fine twined linen)
q: there shall be hangings for the court of fine twined linen one hundred cubits long for one side.

s: court (around the tabernacle) has part pillars (court of the tabernacle) (filleted with silver, sockets of bronze)
q: All the pillars of the court around shall be filleted with silver; their hooks of silver, and their sockets of bronze.

s: court (around the tabernacle) has part gate screen (gate of the court) (twenty cubits, with four pillars)
q: For the gate of the court shall be a screen of twenty cubits, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of the embroiderer; their pillars four, and their sockets four.

s: hangings (court of the tabernacle) is made of fine twined linen
q: there shall be hangings for the court of fine twined linen one hundred cubits long for one side.

s: hangings (court of the tabernacle) has length fifty cubits (west side)
q: For the width of the court on the west side shall be hangings of fifty cubits

s: pure olive oil is used for lamp (beaten oil for light, burning continually)
q: bring to you pure olive oil beaten for the light, to cause a lamp to burn continually.

s: altar has width five cubits
q: You shall make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long, and five cubits wide.

s: children of Israel provides pure olive oil (commanded to bring it)
q: You shall command the children of Israel, that they bring to you pure olive oil beaten for the light

s: Aaron tends lamp (from evening to morning, a statute forever throughout generations)
q: Aaron and his sons shall keep it in order from evening to morning before the LORD: it shall be a statute forever throughout their generations

s: Aaron's sons tends lamp (from evening to morning, a statute forever throughout generations)
q: Aaron and his sons shall keep it in order from evening to morning before the LORD: it shall be a statute forever throughout their generations

s: Tent of Meeting has part veil (lamp kept outside the veil)
q: In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil which is before the covenant

s: altar has shape square
q: The altar shall be square.

s: altar has height three cubits
q: Its height shall be three cubits.

s: altar has part horns (on its four corners, of one piece with it)
q: You shall make its horns on its four corners. Its horns shall be of one piece with it.

s: altar is overlaid with bronze
q: You shall overlay it with bronze.

s: altar has construction hollow with planks
q: You shall make it hollow with planks.

s: altar is made according to mountain (pattern shown on the mountain)
q: They shall make it as it has been shown you on the mountain.

s: Aaron is a brother of Moses (addressed as 'your brother')
q: “Bring Aaron your brother, and his sons with him, near to you from among the children of Israel, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office

s: Aaron's sons has role priest (minister alongside Aaron)
q: They shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother and his sons, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office.

s: Aaron's sons wears tunic (made for them)
q: You shall make tunics for Aaron’s sons.

s: Aaron's sons wears sash (made for them)
q: You shall make sashes for them.

s: Aaron's sons wears linen pants (to cover naked flesh)
q: You shall make them linen pants to cover their naked flesh.

s: Aaron's sons undergoes priesthood ordination (anointed, consecrated, sanctified)
q: and shall anoint them, and consecrate them, and sanctify them, that they may minister to me in the priest’s office.

s: Aaron undergoes priesthood ordination (anointed, consecrated, sanctified)
q: You shall put them on Aaron your brother, and on his sons with him, and shall anoint them, and consecrate them, and sanctify them

s: holy garments (for Aaron and his sons) has purpose glory and beauty
q: You shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother, for glory and for beauty.

s: holy garments (for Aaron and his sons) has purpose sanctify Aaron
q: that they make Aaron’s garments to sanctify him

s: holy garments (for Aaron and his sons) includes breastplate (of the ephod)
q: a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, a fitted tunic, a turban, and a sash.

s: holy garments (for Aaron and his sons) includes ephod
q: a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, a fitted tunic, a turban, and a sash.

s: Aaron has role priest (ministers to the LORD)
q: that he may minister to me in the priest’s office

s: holy garments (for Aaron and his sons) includes robe of the ephod
q: a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, a fitted tunic, a turban, and a sash.

s: holy garments (for Aaron and his sons) includes tunic
q: a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, a fitted tunic, a turban, and a sash.

s: holy garments (for Aaron and his sons) includes turban
q: a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, a fitted tunic, a turban, and a sash.

s: holy garments (for Aaron and his sons) includes sash
q: a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, a fitted tunic, a turban, and a sash.

s: holy garments (for Aaron and his sons) made by wise-hearted workers (filled with spirit of wisdom by the LORD)
q: You shall speak to all who are wise-hearted, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, that they make Aaron’s garments to sanctify him

s: wise-hearted workers filled by LORD (with the spirit of wisdom)
q: whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom

s: holy garments (for Aaron and his sons) made of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen
q: They shall use the gold, and the blue, and the purple, and the scarlet, and the fine linen.

s: ephod made of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, fine twined linen (skillful workman's work)
q: They shall make the ephod of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of the skillful workman.

s: ephod has part shoulder straps (two, joined to its ends)
q: It shall have two shoulder straps joined to the two ends of it, that it may be joined together.

s: ephod has part onyx stones (on the shoulder straps, as memorial)
q: You shall put the two stones on the shoulder straps of the ephod, to be stones of memorial for the children of Israel.

s: Aaron has child Nadab
q: Aaron, with Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, Aaron’s sons.

s: ephod has part woven band (same piece and materials as the ephod)
q: The skillfully woven band, which is on it, shall be like its work and of the same piece

s: breastplate (of the ephod) made of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, fine twined linen (like the ephod's work)
q: like the work of the ephod you shall make it; of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, you shall make it.

s: breastplate (of the ephod) has shape square, folded double (a span by a span)
q: It shall be square and folded double; a span shall be its length, and a span its width.

s: breastplate (of the ephod) has part twelve stones (four rows of three, set in gold)
q: You shall set in it settings of stones, four rows of stones

s: breastplate (of the ephod) represents children of Israel (stones engraved with the names of the twelve tribes)
q: The stones shall be according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names

s: breastplate (of the ephod) has part Urim and Thummim
q: You shall put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim

s: Aaron has child Abihu
q: Aaron, with Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, Aaron’s sons.

s: breastplate (of the ephod) is bound to ephod (by rings and a blue lace so it does not swing out)
q: They shall bind the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue

s: breastplate (of the ephod) has part gold rings (on its ends)
q: You shall make on the breastplate two rings of gold, and shall put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.

s: robe of the ephod is a robe of the ephod (all of blue)
q: You shall make the robe of the ephod all of blue.

s: robe of the ephod has part pomegranates and golden bells (alternating around the hem)
q: a golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, around the hem of the robe.

s: robe of the ephod has part head hole (with woven binding so it does not tear)
q: It shall have a hole for the head in the middle of it. It shall have a binding of woven work around its hole

s: robe of the ephod has purpose sound heard so Aaron does not die (when entering and leaving the holy place)
q: its sound shall be heard when he goes in to the holy place before the LORD, and when he comes out, that he not die.

s: Aaron has child Eleazar
q: Aaron, with Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, Aaron’s sons.

s: priesthood ordination has duration forever (statute for Aaron and his offspring)
q: This shall be a statute forever to him and to his offspring after him.

s: Aaron has child Ithamar
q: Aaron, with Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, Aaron’s sons.

s: Aaron bears children of Israel (names on shoulders as memorial before the LORD)
q: Aaron shall bear their names before the LORD on his two shoulders for a memorial.

s: Aaron bears on heart breastplate (of the ephod) (names of the children of Israel, continually)
q: Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment on his heart, when he goes in to the holy place, for a memorial before the LORD continually.
